attractions.name: Kot Diji Fort
attractions.description: A massive 18th-century hilltop fortress built by the Talpur rulers, offering sweeping views over the surrounding plains — one of Sindh's most iconic forts.

attractions.name: Faiz Mahal
attractions.description: The grand palace of the former Khairpur princely state, known for its striking colonial-Mughal architecture.

attractions.name: Tombs of the Talpur Mirs
attractions.description: Ornate royal mausoleums of the Talpur rulers of Khairpur, featuring intricate tilework.

attractions.name: Khairpur Date Farms
attractions.description: Khairpur produces the majority of Pakistan's dates; date palm orchards are a distinctive part of the local landscape, especially at harvest season.

food_places.name: Khairpur Dates Market
food_places.specialty: Fresh and dried dates in dozens of varieties, a signature Khairpur product

transportation.notes: Most common route to the nearest major transport hub

transportation.route: Intercity coach via National Highway N-5
transportation.notes: Direct coach services run daily from the main bus stand
Rickshaws and local vans are the main way to get around town

weather_info.climate_type: Hot, semi-arid to arid climate typical of interior Sindh
weather_info.avoid_months: May to July (extreme heat, often above 40°C)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Mild and pleasant, 10-24°C, best time to visit
Occasional heavy rain, humid, risk of flooding in low areas

travel_tips.tip: Visit Khairpur in the cooler months (November to February) for the most comfortable travel experience.
Intercity buses and shared vans (Suzuki/coaster) are the most common way to reach and travel around the district.
As with most small-town travel in Sindh, arrange accommodation and local guides in advance, especially outside the main town center.

history.founded: Founded in 1783 as the capital of the princely state of Khairpur under the Talpur Mirs
history.city_history: Khairpur was once a semi-autonomous princely state that acceded to Pakistan in 1947. It remains famous for the Faiz Mahal palace, the Talpur royal tombs, and being Pakistan's largest producer of dates (khajoor).
history.province_history: Sindh is home to one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro), and was later ruled by Persian, Arab, and Mughal empires, as well as the Talpur dynasty, before British annexation in 1843 and eventual inclusion in Pakistan in 1947.
